notes: Missouri computes tax separately for each spouse on a married filing combined return: 'A separate tax must be computed for you and your spouse' (instructions PDF p21; Form MO-1040 Lines 29Y/29S and 30Y/30S). Taxable income is split by each spouse's share of Missouri AGI (Line 7 percentages, Line 27). The one printed chart applies to each person's own Missouri taxable income, so it is entered under married_joint as well as single. A combined return is required, not chosen: 'Missouri law requires a combined return for married couples filing together' (instructions PDF p7). The format has no field for tax figured per spouse.

The chart prints one schedule for every filing status, so married_separate and head_of_household are left out, as the schema asks (they use single); qualifying widow(er) uses married_joint, the same schedule.

Section A of the tax chart prints '$0 to $1,313 ... $0', then 2.0% over $1,313 up to 4.7% over $9,191 (top rate). A bracket with rate 0 from 0 is recorded for the first $1,313. The chart rounds its cumulative amounts ($26, $59, $98, $144, $197, $256) to whole dollars; the bands give 26.26, 59.085, 98.475, 144.43, 196.95, 256.035.

Federal income tax deduction (Form MO-1040 Lines 9-13): Line 11 total federal tax times a percentage set by Missouri AGI (Line 6): $25,000 or less 35%; $25,001 to $50,000 25%; $50,001 to $100,000 15%; $100,001 to $125,000 5%; $125,001 or more 0%. At most $5,000, or $10,000 on a married filing combined return (instructions PDF p8 Lines 12-13; Form MO-1040 PDF p2). The format cannot hold this ladder: its steps keep a share of the relief, and these percentages are shares of the federal tax, not of the cap. So amount holds the cap, phase_out holds the one rung it can (nothing is left over 125,000), and the ladder is in condition and in phase_out.as_printed.

Standard deduction: single or married filing separate $15,750, head of household $23,625, married filing combined or qualifying widow(er) $31,500 (Form MO-1040 PDF p2 Line 14; Reference Guide PDF p10). Each box of age 65 or older or blind adds $2,000 for single or head of household and $1,600 for married filing combined, married filing separately or qualifying widow(er) (instructions PDF p8; Reference Guide PDF p10 table: single with 1 box $17,750, married filing separately with 1 box $17,350). 'The Missouri standard deduction equals the allowable federal standard deduction' (Reference Guide PDF p10).

Itemizing: a filer who itemized federally may itemize on Form MO-A Part 2 or take the standard deduction, whichever is higher; one required to itemize federally must itemize; one who took the federal standard deduction cannot itemize (instructions PDF pp 8 and 16). Missouri itemized deductions are federal itemized deductions plus Social Security, railroad retirement, Medicare and self-employment taxes, less net state income taxes (Form MO-A Part 2, PDF p2). Not held as a fixed amount.

The booklet prints no personal exemption and no dependent exemption for single or joint filers. The only exemption amount is the $1,400 'additional exemption' for head of household and qualifying widow(er) (instructions PDF p8 Line 15).

Missouri AGI starts from federal AGI (Form 1040 Line 11a); a negative federal AGI is treated as $0 (Reference Guide PDF p7; instructions PDF p6). Missouri AGI (Line 6) is after the Form MO-A Part 1 subtractions (capital gain, military retirement, railroad retirement, exempt federal interest, business income) and before the Line 8 pension and Social Security exemptions.

Public pension: 'Public pensions are pensions received from any federal, state, or local government.' (instructions PDF p17; Reference Guide PDF p9; Form MO-A PDF p3 Section A). No income test is printed for 2025: the Pension FAQ gives limits ($85,000 / $100,000 / $85,000) under 'Tax years 2023 and prior' only. No age test or contributory-plan test is printed. The FAQ links an eligibility chart (dor.mo.gov/pdf/pension.pdf) that is not in the sources.

Public pension and Social Security: the form reduces the exemption, not the cap. Section A Line 2 is the lesser of the taxable public pension or $47,633; Line 3 is that person's Social Security or disability exemption (Section C Line 3); Line 4 is Line 2 minus Line 3, not below $0. The Pension FAQ agrees: 'If you also claim the social security or social security disability deduction, your public pension exemption will be reduced by that amount.' So a person's pension and Social Security exemptions together come to the larger of the Social Security exemption and the lesser of the pension or $47,633. Example: pension 30,000 and exempt Social Security 20,000 give Line 2 30,000, Line 4 10,000, 30,000 in all.

Pension from another state's government (New York State included): not named anywhere. 'Public pensions are pensions received from any federal, state, or local government' does not limit the word state to Missouri, so public_pension_other_state is listed in the same entry as public_pension. This is a reading of 'any ... state', not a sentence about other states' pensions. No reciprocity rule and no list of paying states was found in the documents.
Survivor Benefit Plan annuity: it 'does not qualify for the military retirement subtraction' but 'does qualify for the public pension exemption' (Pension FAQ).

100 percent disabled: 'If you are 100 percent disabled, you may consider railroad retirement and military retirement benefits as taxable public pension.' (instructions PDF p17 Line 1; Reference Guide PDF p9 words the railroad part only). Both are already subtracted in full on Form MO-A Part 1, so no separate entry is made.

Private pension (Form MO-A Part 3 Section B, PDF p3): Missouri AGI (MO-1040 Line 6) minus taxable Social Security (federal Line 6b) minus $32,000 married filing combined, $25,000 single, head of household or qualifying widow(er), $16,000 married filing separate gives the excess (Lines 1-5). Each spouse's taxable private pension (federal Lines 4b and 5b) is limited to $6,000 (Lines 6-7), the two are added (Line 8), and the one excess is subtracted from the total (Line 9, not below $0). 'The private pension exemption is reduced by one dollar for every dollar that the taxpayer's income exceeds the limitation' (Reference Guide PDF p9).

Roth conversions: the word Roth appears nowhere in the sources. Section B Line 6 takes taxable amounts from federal Lines 4b and 5b and the booklet does not say whether a conversion counts, so roth_conversion is in covers_unclear.

Social Security: 'Missouri does not tax 100% of social security benefits for individuals age 62 or older, and 100% of social security disability benefits, as long as these benefits are included in federal adjusted gross income under IRC §86' (Pension FAQ, tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2024); 'The 2025 deduction amount is 100 percent of the taxable amount' (Reference Guide PDF p9); Form MO-A PDF p3 Section C. The FAQ's income limits are under 'Tax years 2023 and prior' only. Taxable Social Security is allocated between spouses by each spouse's share of the benefits received (instructions PDF p7 and PDF p17 worksheet).
A filer other than married filing combined may not enter amounts on both the Social Security line and the disability line; on a combined return one spouse may use each (instructions PDF p17).

Military retirement: subtracted on Form MO-A Part 1 Line 10, the amount from federal Line 5b; no cap or income test printed (instructions PDF p14; Pension FAQ: 'The taxable military pension is subtracted from federal adjusted gross income on Form MO-A, Part 1, Line 10'). Active duty and inactive duty deductions (MO-1040 Lines 18 and 19) are for pay, not retirement, and are not recorded.

Business income deduction: 20 percent of Missouri-source business income (instructions PDF p16 worksheet; Form MO-A PDF p2 Line 17). Schedule E Part 2 income is recorded as other_income; the schema has no closer kind.

Capital gain: 'a subtraction from your federal adjusted gross income for 100 percent of your federally reported capital gains'; a negative Line 7a is entered as $0 (instructions PDF p16 Line 18; Form MO-A PDF p2 Line 18; Reference Guide PDF p8 lists it). Other gain rules not recorded: 25 percent on sale of low-income housing and 50 percent ESOP gain (instructions PDF p14), farmland sold to a beginning farmer (MO-1040 Line 21).

Municipal interest: Form MO-A Part 1 Line 1 adds 'Interest on state and local obligations other than Missouri source'; no sentence says Missouri-source interest is exempt, it is simply not added. Recorded as other_states_taxed_own_exempt on that basis.

US obligations: 'Interest from direct obligations of the U.S. Government ... is exempt from state taxation under the laws of the United States' (instructions PDF p13 Line 8). Related expenses reduce the amount claimed when over $500.

Other subtractions and deductions not recorded as reliefs: state income tax refund (Line 9), Build America and Recovery Zone bond interest and other Line 11 items, 529 and ABLE contributions (Lines 12 and 15), qualified health insurance premiums (Line 13), agriculture disaster relief (Line 16), long-term care insurance (MO-1040 Line 16), health care sharing ministry (Line 17), foster parent (Line 24). Credits not recorded: resident credit for tax paid to another state (Form MO-CR), property tax credit, Missouri Working Family Tax Credit. Line 34 adds a tax of 10 percent of the federal Form 4972 tax on a lump sum distribution (instructions PDF pp 9-10).

Indexing: no sentence on inflation adjustment of brackets, the $6,000 private cap or the income limits was found in any document. The public pension cap is the maximum Social Security benefit, which the Pension FAQ lists by tax year ($46,381 for 2024, $47,633 for 2025, $48,967 for 2026).
No surtax or recapture is printed.
Not found in the booklet: any age-based deduction against all income, any separate rule for Roth conversions, any rule for a pension paid by another state's government beyond the words quoted above.
